title: Officer Avila is back! The Blue Notebook Review
description:
In this week's edition of the Blue Notebook Review, Sergeant Verbeck and the Neighborhood Resource Officers (NROs) provide a comprehensive update on public safety and community initiatives across Santa Monica.

In this episode, we cover:
Homelessness Outreach: Officer Tago discusses recent statistics and a successful relocation story involving a mother and daughter. 

Crime Suppression: Officer Hollowell reports on recent arrests and reminds residents to use the non-emergency line: 310-458-8491.

Traffic Safety: Officer Pardo highlights enforcement in school zones and high-collision corridors.

Community Engagement: Officer Avila previews upcoming neighborhood meetings and our "Compression with a Cop" event on March 12th!


Video Chapters
[00:00:01] – Introduction with Sergeant Verbeck
[00:00:15] – Homelessness Outreach update and relocation success story (Officer Tago)
[00:01:10] – Crime Suppression and non-emergency reporting (Officer Hollowell)
[00:02:18] – Traffic Safety: Enforcement in school zones and collision corridors (Officer Pardo)
[00:03:30] – Community Engagement: Upcoming meetings and "Compression with a Cop" (Officer Avila)
[00:04:45] – Closing remarks and how to stay connected

📌 STAY CONNECTED:
Follow us for more updates on how we are working to keep Santa Monica safe.

Website: www.santamonica.gov/police
Instagram: @SantaMonicaPD
X: @SantaMonicaPD

🔔 Subscribe to our channel to never miss a weekly update!

#SantaMonica #SMPD #PublicSafety #CommunityPolicing #BlueNotebookReview #NRO #SantaMonicaPolice

Aloha, Santa Monica. Officer Tago here, your B3 neighborhood resource officer. Homeless related calls continue to represent a significant portion of service demand during this reporting period. Officers recorded 573 homeless related dispositions and responded to 21 encampment calls across the entire city. Patrol and specialized units conducted periodic checks in Tongva, Reed, and Palis parks with a focus on addressing violations and working toward long-term solutions in those areas. And here's the help team stats for this last reporting period. Our homeless lay program officers responded to 115 radio calls, conducted 99 proactive stops, addressed nine encampments, made 31 arrest, and issued 18 citations, and also conducted five mental health evaluations. And here's your incident of note. Your neighborhood resource officers responded to a verbal dispute in the 2400 block of Oak Street after a reporting party stated she was being yelled at by individuals living inside a vehicle. Officers determined no crime had occurred. However, during the investigation, they discovered an adult female living in the vehicle with her 15-year-old daughter, and both appear to be malnourished. The mother made several delusional statements indicating the government was targeting her daughter and that others intended to harm her and her daughter. Based on those statements and the living conditions, officers requested a department of mental health clinician come out and conduct an evaluation. The subject ultimately met criteria for a mental health hold and was transported to UCLA Westwood for evaluation. The daughter was transported to headquarters while officers contacted DCFS who later responded and assumed custody of the child. While waiting for DCFS to arrive, community engagement personnel remain with the child and provide support. It's situations like this that highlight the balance of work enforcement when necessary while also stepping in to protect vulnerable individuals and connect them with the help that they need. We'll keep showing up. We'll keep addressing issues directly and we'll keep working alongside our partners to keep the community safe. from out here in beautiful Santa Monica. For this operational period for crime suppression, officers responded to 24,426 calls for service as well as conducted 96 arrests. I will discuss two incidents. The first being the Franklin Avenue death investigation. Awatch patrol responded to a down person along with the Santa Monica Fire Department. The fire department pronounced the person deceased at scene. The Criminal Investigations Division detectives responded to the scene as well as the LA County corner. Preliminary investigation revealed that it was a accidental overdose. For the second incident, multiple officers made multiple arrests at locations. Those units being the crime impact team as well as patrol and the downtown services unit. Those persons arrested were arrested for multiple parole and probation violations as well as narcotics arrests. This was done in the Pico corridor as well as the downtown area. Great bang up job. Way to work the beat, Santa Monica. And on another note, I would like to remind you all that the way to contact the police when you see something, I want you to say something. Please do not contact 311. I would like you to call 310-458-88491 to identify any problems to us so that we can readily respond quickly to identify the problem and make arrests appropriately. And as always, in emergency, call 911. And it's back to you in the studio, Sergeant Verbeck. >> Thanks, Officer Hollowell. I too can keep it official, but that's not my style. So, let's hear from your B2 NRO, Izzy, who's going to talk to you about our traffic enforcement efforts. Izzy, the floor is yours. >> Hi, Santa Monica. Traffic enforcement remained active this week with officers focusing on school zones, Pacific Coast Highway, downtown Santa Monica, and other high collision corridors. Operations included traffic directed enforcement and school dropoff monitoring, pedestrian and bicycle efforts, and crash investigations with added visibility in areas generating community complaints. This week, officers conducted 315 traffic stops and issued 195 citations, both up from last week. A few moments that made the traffic log interesting. At Second and Broadway, a juvenile driver decided red lights were more of a suggestion and ran several of them before colliding with multiple vehicles. Several people were injured. The driver was cited and released to their parents, who likely had a much longer conversation waiting at home. Officers also contacted three miners riding motorcycles on the Third Street prominade. As it turns out, the prominade is only for walking, shopping, and people watching, not motorcycles. The riders were cited and the motorcycles were impounded. Meanwhile, school zone enforcement continued near Lincoln Middle School, Santa Monica High School, and Roosevelt Elementary in a grant-f funded pedestrian and bicycle safety operation resulted in 12 citations. Remember, traffic laws aren't suggestions. They're there. so everyone gets home safely. Back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Thanks, Izzy. And I'm being told here that your beat four in a row, Brandon, is reporting live from an undisclosed location in an attempt to conceal his whereabouts from internal affairs. Uh, Brandon, if that's really you, what do you have for us? >> Thank you, sir. Hello, Blue Noel family. Serge, I think they know it's me. you can remove the bar >> plus have to drive. So during this reporting period, the community engagement team participated in multiple neighborhood meetings citywide. We provided crime data and we also addressed quality of life issues in the areas. Our youth outreach included a presentation at Grant Elementary in partnership with our animal control department. We also conducted business engagement security assessments and also provided them crime data and came up with resolutions for issues in their neighborhoods. We remain busy on social media. I hope you're following us, liking us, and please leave a good comment. Most importantly, March 12th, it's a Thursday, 10:00 a.m. We'll be at Restore Hyper Wellness at 10:31 Montana for Compression with the Cop. I hope you can make it out there. It's all I have for this week. Back to you in the studio, Sarge. Yeah, >> looks like Brandon's doing well after all. Hey, can you cancel the bolo for Brandon? Thank you.
